_help: College majors for the College & Career Finder and the /college-majors/ pages. fields: groups of majors. Each major: summary (one sentence), about (a short paragraph), study (typical courses), skills, degrees (typical award levels), careers (CEI career slugs, most relevant first: they drive career suggestions and training recommendations), minors ([minor slug, why it pairs well]), interests (interest slugs from interests.json), cip (federal CIP program codes or prefixes, used to find colleges that report awarding this major in IPEDS), aka (other names visitors search for). Keep descriptions general and factual: no salaries, admission requirements or outcomes.

fields.name: Healthcare
fields.blurb: Majors that prepare you to care for patients, run health organizations or work behind the scenes in medicine.

fields.name: Business
fields.blurb: Majors in management, marketing, accounting, finance and the other functions every organization needs.

fields.name: Technology
fields.blurb: Majors in computing, software, data, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence.

fields.name: Engineering and Architecture
fields.blurb: Majors that apply math and science to design machines, structures, circuits and systems.

fields.name: Construction and Skilled Trades
fields.blurb: Majors and technical programs for building, wiring, heating, cooling and managing construction.

fields.name: Manufacturing and Mechanics
fields.blurb: Programs in machining, automation, and vehicle and aircraft maintenance.

fields.name: Transportation and Logistics
fields.blurb: Majors that keep goods and people moving, from supply chains to aviation.

fields.name: Education
fields.blurb: Majors for teaching children, teens and adults and designing how people learn.

fields.name: Science and Mathematics
fields.blurb: Majors in the natural sciences, laboratory science and mathematics.

fields.name: Criminal Justice, Law and Public Safety
fields.blurb: Majors for law enforcement, fire and emergency services and legal careers.

fields.name: Communications and Media
fields.blurb: Majors in communication, journalism, public relations, writing and digital media.

fields.name: Arts and Design
fields.blurb: Majors in visual design, interior and fashion design, fine arts and music.

fields.name: Hospitality, Culinary and Tourism
fields.blurb: Majors for hotels, restaurants, events, recreation and travel.

fields.name: Psychology, Social Sciences and Public Service
fields.blurb: Majors that study people and communities and prepare you to serve them.

fields.name: Environment, Safety and Sustainability
fields.blurb: Majors in environmental science, workplace safety and clean energy.

fields.name: Agriculture and Natural Resources
fields.blurb: Majors in farming, animal science, forestry and conservation.

majors.name: Nursing
majors.summary: Prepares you to assess, treat and educate patients as part of a healthcare team.
majors.about: Nursing programs combine science courses with supervised clinical experience in hospitals and other care settings. Graduates of an approved registered nursing program (an associate degree in nursing or a bachelor of science in nursing) can take the NCLEX-RN exam for state licensure. Practical nursing certificates lead to the NCLEX-PN, and graduate nursing degrees prepare nurse practitioners, nurse anesthetists and nurse educators.
study: Pediatric, maternal and mental health nursing
majors.degrees: Practical nursing certificate, associate degree (ADN), bachelor's degree (BSN), and master's and doctoral degrees for advanced practice
minors: Helps you understand patient behavior, mental health and how people cope with illness.
Adds a community view of disease prevention that fits public health and school nursing.
Builds management and policy knowledge for charge nurse and nurse manager roles.
Lets you communicate directly with Spanish-speaking patients and families.
Focuses on the care of older adults, a large and growing share of patients.

majors.name: Healthcare Administration
majors.summary: Teaches you to manage the business side of hospitals, clinics and health systems.
majors.about: Healthcare administration combines business courses with health policy, law and ethics. Students learn how health organizations are financed, staffed, regulated and measured on quality. Entry roles are often in medical offices, billing and patient services, with management roles following experience; many health system executives also hold a master's degree.
majors.degrees: Bachelor's degree, with a master's (MHA or MBA) common for senior management
minors: Strengthens general management, finance and operations skills.
Helps with budgets, reimbursement and the financial reports administrators review.
Connects administration to population health and community programs.
Prepares you to measure quality, costs and patient outcomes.
Helps with staffing, hiring and retention, major challenges in healthcare.
majors.aka: health administration, health services management, healthcare management, MHA

majors.name: Public Health
majors.summary: Studies how to prevent disease and improve the health of whole communities.
majors.about: Public health majors learn how diseases spread, how health is shaped by environment and behavior, and how programs and policies protect populations. Coursework includes epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental health and health education. Graduates work in health departments, hospitals, nonprofits and workplace health and safety; research and epidemiologist roles usually require a master's degree.
majors.degrees: Bachelor's degree, with a master's (MPH) common for epidemiology and program leadership
minors: Builds the quantitative skills behind epidemiology and program evaluation.
Deepens your understanding of disease, infection and the human body.
Explains the social conditions that shape health in communities.
Connects public health to air, water and environmental hazards.
Helps you reach and serve Spanish-speaking communities.

majors.name: Health Sciences
majors.summary: A broad science-based major that prepares you for clinical programs and health careers.
majors.about: Health sciences programs cover biology, anatomy, health care delivery and research, and many students use the major to prepare for graduate programs in physical therapy, occupational therapy, physician assistant studies, pharmacy or medicine. Others go directly into health education, administration or research support roles.
majors.degrees: Associate and bachelor's degrees, often followed by a graduate clinical program
minors: Useful for nearly every patient-facing role and many graduate programs.
Covers prerequisites many clinical graduate programs require.
Adds a prevention and population perspective.
Fits physical therapy, athletic training and wellness careers.
majors.aka: pre-health, pre-med, allied health, health studies

majors.name: Medical Assisting
majors.summary: A short program that prepares you for clinical and administrative work in medical offices.
majors.about: Medical assisting programs, offered as certificates and associate degrees, teach both front-office tasks such as scheduling and billing and back-office clinical tasks such as taking vital signs, preparing patients and assisting providers. Many programs include an externship, and graduates may sit for national medical assistant certification exams.
minors: Prepares you for office lead and practice management roles.
Medical offices often need bilingual staff to support patients.
Helps you work with anxious or upset patients.
majors.aka: medical assistant, CMA, clinical medical assistant

majors.name: Health Information Management
majors.summary: Teaches you to manage, protect and code patient health records and data.
majors.about: Health information management (HIM) sits where healthcare meets data. Students learn medical coding systems, health data privacy rules such as HIPAA, electronic health records, and how health data supports billing and quality reporting. Associate programs lead to technician roles, and bachelor's programs prepare students for HIM management.
minors: Helps you support the systems that store health records.
Prepares you to turn health data into reports and insights.
Adds management skills for department supervisor roles.
majors.aka: HIM, health informatics, medical records, medical coding, medical billing

majors.name: Radiologic Technology and Medical Imaging
majors.summary: Prepares you to create medical images such as X-rays, CT, MRI and ultrasound.
majors.about: Medical imaging programs teach anatomy, patient positioning, radiation safety and the operation of imaging equipment, with extensive clinical practice. Graduates of accredited programs can sit for certification exams such as those from the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists, and many states license radiologic technologists.
minors: Strengthens your understanding of how imaging equipment and radiation work.
Prepares you to lead an imaging department later in your career.
Helps you calm and reassure patients during procedures.
majors.aka: radiography, X-ray tech, sonography, ultrasound, MRI, medical imaging

majors.name: Respiratory Therapy
majors.summary: Prepares you to evaluate and treat patients with breathing and heart-lung problems.
majors.about: Respiratory therapy programs teach cardiopulmonary anatomy, ventilator management, airway care and diagnostic testing, with clinical rotations in intensive care and emergency settings. Graduates of accredited programs can earn credentials from the National Board for Respiratory Care, and nearly every state licenses respiratory therapists.
minors: Deepens your knowledge of the body systems you treat.
Prepares you for department lead roles.
Many respiratory patients are older adults with chronic disease.

majors.name: Emergency Medical Services
majors.summary: Trains you to provide emergency care at the scene and during transport.
majors.about: EMS programs range from short EMT courses to paramedic certificates and associate degrees. Students learn patient assessment, airway management, trauma and cardiac care, and emergency operations, with ambulance and hospital clinical time. EMTs and paramedics need state certification, often based on National Registry exams.
majors.degrees: EMT and paramedic certificates and associate degrees
minors: Adds disaster planning and incident command knowledge.
Helps you communicate with patients in an emergency.
Helps you manage stress and support people in crisis.

majors.name: Kinesiology and Exercise Science
majors.summary: Studies human movement, exercise and physical activity for health and performance.
majors.about: Kinesiology and exercise science majors study anatomy, biomechanics, exercise physiology and motor learning. The major often leads to fitness and wellness careers or serves as preparation for graduate programs in physical therapy, occupational therapy, athletic training or exercise physiology.
majors.degrees: Bachelor's degree, with graduate degrees for clinical professions
minors: Pairs exercise with diet, a natural fit for wellness careers.
Helps you understand motivation and behavior change.
Useful if you plan to run a gym or training business.
majors.aka: exercise science, kinesiology, physical education, sports medicine

majors.name: Nutrition and Dietetics
majors.summary: Studies food, nutrients and diet and how they affect health and disease.
majors.about: Nutrition and dietetics majors learn biochemistry, food science, medical nutrition therapy and community nutrition. Becoming a registered dietitian nutritionist requires an accredited program, supervised practice, a national exam and, as of 2024, a graduate degree; many states also license dietitians.
majors.degrees: Bachelor's degree, with a master's degree now required to become a registered dietitian
minors: Connects nutrition with fitness and sports performance.
Helps with counseling and long-term behavior change.
Strengthens the biochemistry behind nutrition science.
Fits foodservice and institutional dining management.
majors.aka: dietetics, nutrition science, dietitian, food and nutrition

majors.name: Dental Hygiene and Dental Assisting
majors.summary: Prepares you to clean teeth, take X-rays and support dentists in patient care.
majors.about: Dental assisting programs are usually certificates, while dental hygiene programs are typically associate degrees, with bachelor's options. Students learn oral anatomy, radiography, infection control and preventive care in clinics. Dental hygienists must be licensed in every state, and many states regulate the tasks dental assistants may perform.
minors: Fits community and school dental health programs.
Useful for office management or practice ownership later.

majors.name: Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
majors.summary: Studies medications: how they work, how they are made and how they are dispensed safely.
majors.about: Pharmacy-related programs range from pharmacy technician certificates to bachelor's degrees in pharmaceutical sciences and the Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) required to practice as a pharmacist. Pharmacists must pass licensing exams, and most states register or certify pharmacy technicians.
majors.degrees: Pharmacy technician certificate, bachelor's in pharmaceutical sciences, Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD)
minors: Builds the chemistry foundation behind how drugs work.
Useful for pharmacy management and retail operations.
Helps you counsel patients about their medications.
majors.aka: pharmacy technician, pharmaceutical science, PharmD, pharmacist

majors.name: Surgical Technology
majors.summary: Prepares you to set up operating rooms and assist surgeons during procedures.
majors.about: Surgical technology programs teach sterile technique, surgical instruments, anatomy and operating room procedures, with clinical rotations in surgery departments. Some states require certification, which graduates of accredited programs can earn through national exams.
minors: Strengthens your anatomy and microbiology knowledge.
Prepares you for operating room coordinator roles.
majors.aka: surgical tech, scrub tech, operating room technician

majors.name: Medical Laboratory Science
majors.summary: Prepares you to run the lab tests doctors use to diagnose and treat disease.
majors.about: Medical laboratory science programs cover clinical chemistry, hematology, microbiology, immunology and blood banking, with practice in hospital labs. Associate programs prepare medical laboratory technicians, and bachelor's programs prepare medical laboratory scientists; some states license laboratory personnel.
minors: Supports the chemistry behind many lab tests.
Helps with lab quality data and reporting.
Deepens your knowledge of disease and the human body.
majors.aka: clinical laboratory science, medical technology, MLT, MLS, lab tech

majors.name: Business Administration
majors.summary: A broad business major that covers management, finance, marketing and operations.
majors.about: Business administration gives you a working knowledge of how organizations run. Students take core courses in accounting, finance, marketing, management, business law and statistics, then often choose a concentration. The major is flexible: graduates work in nearly every industry, and it is a common starting point for an MBA later.
majors.degrees: Associate and bachelor's degrees, plus the MBA
minors: Gives you the financial literacy managers rely on every day.
Helps you understand customers and how businesses grow.
Prepares you to base decisions on data, a skill employers ask for across business roles.
Gives you a structured way to plan and deliver work.
Sharpens the writing and presentation skills business leaders use constantly.
majors.aka: business, BBA, business management, commerce, MBA

majors.name: Marketing
majors.summary: Studies how organizations understand customers and promote products and services.
majors.about: Marketing majors learn consumer behavior, market research, branding, advertising, digital and social media marketing, and sales. Many programs now emphasize analytics and digital tools. Graduates work in agencies, corporate marketing teams, nonprofits and sales organizations.
minors: Strengthens writing and messaging for campaigns.
Explains why people buy and how they make decisions.
Adds a broader view of finance and operations.
Lets you create the visuals behind campaigns.
Prepares you to measure campaign results.
majors.aka: advertising, digital marketing, brand management, social media marketing

majors.name: Accounting
majors.summary: Teaches you to record, analyze, report and audit financial information.
majors.about: Accounting majors learn financial and managerial accounting, tax, auditing and accounting information systems. Becoming a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) requires meeting a state's education and experience requirements and passing the CPA exam; many states require 150 semester hours of education. Accounting graduates work in public accounting firms, businesses, government and nonprofits.
minors: Adds investment and corporate finance knowledge.
Prepares you for accounting technology and audit of IT systems.
Prepares you for data-driven auditing and analysis.
Helps with tax law, contracts and compliance.

majors.name: Finance
majors.summary: Studies how individuals and organizations raise, invest and manage money.
majors.about: Finance majors learn corporate finance, investments, financial markets, banking and risk management, using quantitative tools and financial software. Graduates work in banks, investment and insurance firms, corporate finance departments and government. Some roles require licenses or professional certifications.
minors: Explains the economic forces behind markets and rates.
Helps you read and analyze financial statements.
Strengthens the quantitative skills behind modeling.
Prepares you for analytics-heavy finance roles.
majors.aka: banking, investments, financial planning, corporate finance

majors.name: Human Resources Management
majors.summary: Teaches you to recruit, train, pay and support an organization's workforce.
majors.about: Human resources majors study staffing, training and development, compensation and benefits, employment law and employee relations. Graduates work in HR departments of all kinds of organizations, and many later pursue professional certifications.
minors: Explains motivation, behavior and workplace dynamics.
Strengthens the communication HR relies on.
Connects HR to finance and strategy.
Deepens your knowledge of employment law.
majors.aka: HR, human resources, personnel, talent management

majors.name: Entrepreneurship
majors.summary: Teaches you to start, fund and grow a new business or venture.
majors.about: Entrepreneurship majors learn to spot opportunities, test ideas, write business plans, raise money and manage a small business. Courses usually combine business fundamentals with hands-on projects and pitch competitions.
minors: Helps you find and win your first customers.
Lets you manage your own books and cash flow.
Helps you build a brand online.
Covers contracts, liability and business formation.
majors.aka: small business, startups, innovation, business ownership

majors.name: Management and Organizational Leadership
majors.summary: Focuses on leading people, teams and organizations.
majors.about: Management and organizational leadership majors study leadership, organizational behavior, strategy, change management and ethics. The major suits students who want to supervise teams in any industry, and it is popular with working adults moving into supervisory roles.
minors: Helps you hire, develop and keep good people.
Gives you tools for planning and delivering work.
Strengthens the communication leaders rely on.

majors.name: Economics
majors.summary: Studies how people, businesses and governments make choices about scarce resources.
majors.about: Economics majors learn microeconomics, macroeconomics and econometrics, using math and data to analyze markets, policy and behavior. Graduates work in finance, consulting, government and research, and the major is good preparation for law school and graduate study.
minors: Prepares you for data-heavy analyst roles.
Applies economics to markets and investing.

majors.name: Project Management
majors.summary: Teaches you to plan, schedule, budget and deliver projects of any kind.
majors.about: Project management programs cover project planning, scheduling, cost control, risk management and team leadership, along with both traditional and agile methods. The skills apply in construction, IT, healthcare, marketing and government, and many professionals later earn project management certifications.
minors: Connects projects to finance and strategy.
Prepares you to manage IT and software projects.
Applies project skills on construction sites.

majors.name: Business Analytics
majors.summary: Teaches you to use data and statistics to answer business questions.
majors.about: Business analytics majors learn statistics, data management, visualization and predictive modeling, applied to marketing, operations and finance problems. Students use tools such as spreadsheets, SQL and analytics software to turn data into recommendations.
minors: Adds programming for more advanced analysis.
Applies analytics to customers and campaigns.
Applies analytics to investments and planning.
majors.aka: analytics, business intelligence, data analytics, management science

majors.name: Real Estate
majors.summary: Studies how property is bought, sold, financed, developed and managed.
majors.about: Real estate majors learn property law, valuation, finance, investment and property management. Selling real estate requires a state license, which has its own prelicensing coursework and exam; a degree is not required for licensure, but it can help in commercial real estate, development and finance.
minors: Helps you win and serve clients.
Useful for development and renovation projects.
majors.aka: realtor, property management, real estate finance

majors.name: Insurance and Risk Management
majors.summary: Studies how risks are measured, priced and covered by insurance.
majors.about: Insurance and risk management majors learn underwriting, claims, risk analysis, insurance law and financial planning. Graduates work for insurers, agencies and corporate risk departments. Selling insurance requires a state license.
minors: Connects insurance to investments and financial planning.
Builds the math behind pricing risk.
Helps with policy contracts and claims disputes.

majors.name: International Business
majors.summary: Studies how companies trade, operate and compete across countries.
majors.about: International business majors combine business fundamentals with global trade, international finance, cross-cultural management and often a foreign language. Graduates work in importing and exporting, global supply chains, multinational companies and government trade agencies.
minors: Adds a language widely used in international trade.
Covers the logistics of moving goods across borders.
Explains trade, exchange rates and global markets.
majors.aka: global business, international trade, import export

majors.name: Sales and Merchandising
majors.summary: Teaches professional selling, retail management and merchandising.
majors.about: Sales and merchandising programs cover professional selling, customer relationship management, retail operations, buying and visual merchandising. Graduates work in business-to-business sales, retail management and wholesale distribution.
minors: Connects selling to the wider marketing plan.
majors.aka: sales, retail management, merchandising, professional selling

majors.name: Computer Science
majors.summary: Studies how computers and software work and how to design programs that solve problems.
majors.about: Computer science majors learn programming, data structures, algorithms, computer architecture, operating systems and theory, with electives in areas such as artificial intelligence, security and software engineering. It is math-intensive and prepares graduates for software development and for graduate study.
study: Programming in languages such as Python, Java or C++
majors.degrees: Associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees
minors: Strengthens the math behind algorithms, graphics and AI.
Helps you understand the problems software is built to solve and prepares you for tech leadership.
Adds secure coding and defense skills employers value.
Focuses your electives on machine learning and AI.

majors.name: Information Technology
majors.summary: Focuses on setting up, running and supporting the computer systems organizations depend on.
majors.about: Information technology programs are more applied than computer science. Students learn networking, operating systems, system administration, databases, cloud services, security and help-desk support. Many programs build toward industry certifications, and graduates support users and infrastructure in every industry.
minors: Builds security skills every IT role now needs.
Prepares you to manage IT budgets and teams.
Helps you lead upgrades and rollouts.
majors.aka: IT, networking, help desk, system administration, computer support

majors.name: Cybersecurity
majors.summary: Teaches you to protect computer systems, networks and data from attacks.
majors.about: Cybersecurity majors learn network security, ethical hacking, digital forensics, cryptography, security policy and incident response. Hands-on labs are common, and many students prepare for industry security certifications. Graduates work in security operations, IT, government and consulting.
majors.degrees: Certificate, associate, bachelor's and master's degrees
minors: Adds programming depth for security engineering.
Covers privacy law and compliance requirements.
majors.aka: cyber security, information security, infosec, ethical hacking

majors.name: Data Science and Analytics
majors.summary: Combines statistics, programming and domain knowledge to find insights in data.
majors.about: Data science majors learn statistics, programming, data management, machine learning and visualization, then apply them to real data sets. The field overlaps with computer science and statistics, and graduates work as analysts and data scientists in business, healthcare, government and technology.
majors.degrees: Bachelor's and master's degrees, plus certificates
minors: Helps you apply data to business decisions.
Applies data science to health questions.
majors.aka: data analytics, data analysis, big data, analytics

majors.name: Artificial Intelligence
majors.summary: Studies how to build computer systems that learn, reason and understand language and images.
majors.about: Artificial intelligence majors, a newer offering at many colleges, build on computer science and mathematics. Students study machine learning, neural networks, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics and the ethics of AI. Graduates work in software and data roles that build or apply AI systems.
minors: AI depends heavily on linear algebra, calculus and statistics.
Prepares you to weigh fairness, privacy and safety questions in AI.
Connects AI to how people think, learn and use technology.
Helps you apply AI to real business problems.
majors.aka: AI, machine learning, ML, deep learning

majors.name: Information Systems
majors.summary: Connects business and technology: how organizations choose, build and use information systems.
majors.about: Information systems majors, often housed in business schools as management information systems (MIS), study databases, systems analysis, business processes, project management and IT strategy. Graduates often act as translators between business teams and technical teams.
minors: Fits accounting information systems and IT audit roles.
Adds analysis to your systems skills.
Adds security, a growing part of systems work.
majors.aka: MIS, management information systems, CIS, computer information systems

majors.name: Software Engineering
majors.summary: Applies engineering methods to designing, building, testing and maintaining software.
majors.about: Software engineering majors learn programming plus the practices teams use to deliver reliable software: requirements, design, testing, version control and project management. Many programs include team projects with real clients.
minors: Prepares you for product and leadership roles.
Teaches you to build secure software.

majors.name: Web Design and Development
majors.summary: Teaches you to design and build websites and web applications.
majors.about: Web design and development programs cover HTML, CSS, JavaScript, user experience design, accessibility and the back-end systems that power websites. Programs range from certificates to bachelor's degrees and usually ask students to build a portfolio.
minors: Strengthens the visual side of web design.
Connects websites to digital marketing goals.
Adds programming depth for complex applications.
majors.aka: web design, front-end development, UX, web developer

majors.name: Mechanical Engineering
majors.summary: Designs machines, engines, tools and mechanical systems.
majors.about: Mechanical engineering is one of the broadest engineering fields. Students study mechanics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, materials and machine design, and use computer-aided design and simulation. Graduates work in manufacturing, energy, automotive, aerospace and many other industries; professional licensure is available after experience and exams.
minors: Prepares you for engineering management roles.
Adds programming for automation and simulation.
Applies engineering to energy efficiency and clean technology.

majors.name: Electrical Engineering
majors.summary: Designs electrical systems, electronics, power and communications equipment.
majors.about: Electrical engineering majors study circuits, electronics, signals, electromagnetics, power systems and digital systems. Graduates work in power utilities, electronics, telecommunications, manufacturing and defense.
minors: Helps with embedded systems and programming.
Supports signal processing and control theory.

majors.name: Civil Engineering
majors.summary: Designs roads, bridges, buildings, water systems and other infrastructure.
majors.about: Civil engineering majors study structures, geotechnics, transportation, water resources and construction. Graduates work for engineering firms, contractors and government agencies, and professional engineer (PE) licensure is common for those who approve designs.
minors: Connects design with how projects get built.
Fits water, stormwater and environmental projects.
Adds mapping and spatial analysis used in infrastructure planning.

majors.name: Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering
majors.summary: Improves how people, machines, materials and information work together.
majors.about: Industrial engineering majors study operations research, statistics, quality control, ergonomics, supply chains and manufacturing processes. Graduates make factories, hospitals, warehouses and service operations more efficient and safer.
minors: Connects efficiency work to costs and strategy.
Applies your skills to logistics and distribution.
Adds ergonomics and workplace safety expertise.
majors.aka: IE, manufacturing engineering, process engineering, lean

majors.name: Chemical Engineering
majors.summary: Designs processes that turn raw materials into fuels, chemicals, medicines and products.
majors.about: Chemical engineering majors study chemistry, thermodynamics, transport phenomena, reaction engineering and process design. Graduates work in chemicals, energy, pharmaceuticals, food processing and environmental protection.
minors: Process safety is central to chemical plants.
Fits pollution control and sustainability work.

majors.name: Aerospace Engineering
majors.summary: Designs aircraft, spacecraft, satellites and missiles.
majors.about: Aerospace engineering majors study aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, flight mechanics and control systems. Graduates work for aircraft and space manufacturers, airlines, government agencies and defense contractors.
minors: Adds programming for simulation and flight software.
Deepens your understanding of flight and space.

majors.name: Biomedical Engineering
majors.summary: Applies engineering to medicine: devices, implants, imaging and diagnostics.
majors.about: Biomedical engineering majors combine engineering with biology and physiology to design medical devices, prosthetics, imaging systems and lab equipment. Graduates work in medical device companies, hospitals and research, and some continue to medical or graduate school.
minors: Deepens the life science side of the field.
Helps with product development and regulation.

majors.name: Computer Engineering
majors.summary: Designs computer hardware and the software that runs closest to it.
majors.about: Computer engineering blends electrical engineering and computer science. Students study digital logic, computer architecture, embedded systems, networks and programming, and graduates design processors, devices, networks and embedded software.
minors: Fits hardware and embedded security work.
majors.aka: CompE, computer hardware engineering, embedded systems

majors.name: Environmental Engineering
majors.summary: Designs systems that protect air, water and land from pollution.
majors.about: Environmental engineering majors study water and wastewater treatment, air quality, hazardous waste, environmental chemistry and regulations. Graduates work for consulting firms, utilities, industry and government agencies.
minors: Broadens your view of clean energy and resource use.
Connects environmental work to worker protection and hazardous waste.

majors.name: Engineering Technology
majors.summary: An applied, hands-on engineering degree focused on building, testing and maintaining systems.
majors.about: Engineering technology programs emphasize applying engineering principles more than theory. Students specialize in areas such as electrical, mechanical, civil or drafting and design technology, with lots of lab work. Associate graduates often work as technicians, and bachelor's graduates as technologists or applied engineers.
minors: Prepares you to supervise technical teams.
Adds safety knowledge for plants and job sites.
majors.aka: engineering technician, drafting, CAD, applied engineering

majors.name: Architecture
majors.summary: Designs buildings and spaces that are useful, safe and beautiful.
majors.about: Architecture programs teach design studio, building technology, structures, history and theory, and digital design tools. Becoming a licensed architect requires a degree from an accredited professional program, supervised experience and passing the Architect Registration Examination.
majors.degrees: Bachelor's (including five-year professional degrees) and master's degrees
minors: Fits green building and energy-efficient design.
Useful for running a design practice.

majors.name: Construction Management
majors.summary: Teaches you to plan, budget, schedule and supervise construction projects.
majors.about: Construction management majors study construction methods and materials, estimating, scheduling, contracts, safety and project management. Graduates work for general contractors, specialty contractors, developers and owners, often starting as project engineers or assistant superintendents.
majors.degrees: Certificate, associate, bachelor's and master's degrees
minors: Prepares you to manage budgets and run a contracting business.
Adds formal planning and scheduling methods.
Construction is high-risk, so safety knowledge is valued on every site.
majors.aka: construction manager, construction science, building construction

majors.name: Building Science and Construction Technology
majors.summary: Studies how buildings are designed, built and maintained to perform well.
majors.about: Building science and construction technology programs cover building systems, materials, energy efficiency, codes and inspection. Graduates work as technicians, inspectors, estimators and building performance specialists.
minors: Fits green building and energy work.
Useful for running a contracting or inspection business.
majors.aka: construction technology, building technology, architectural technology

majors.name: Industrial Technology
majors.summary: Prepares you to manage and improve industrial and manufacturing operations.
majors.about: Industrial technology programs combine technical courses in manufacturing processes, automation, quality and safety with management skills. Graduates work as technicians, supervisors and technical managers in manufacturing and industrial settings.
minors: Adds the safety knowledge plants depend on.
Connects production to purchasing and logistics.
majors.aka: industrial tech, manufacturing technology, industrial management

majors.name: Welding Technology
majors.summary: Teaches you to join and cut metal using welding processes used in industry.
majors.about: Welding programs teach shielded metal arc, gas metal arc, flux-cored and gas tungsten arc welding, plus blueprint reading, metallurgy and safety. Many prepare students for welding certification tests, such as those based on American Welding Society codes.
minors: Helps if you plan to run your own welding shop.
Welding hazards make safety knowledge valuable.

majors.name: Electrical Technology
majors.summary: Prepares you to install, maintain and troubleshoot electrical systems.
majors.about: Electrical technology programs teach electrical theory, the National Electrical Code, residential and commercial wiring, motor controls and safety. Graduates often enter apprenticeships, which together with exams lead to state or local electrician licensing.
minors: Prepares you for solar and energy storage work.
Useful for becoming an electrical contractor.

majors.name: HVAC Technology
majors.summary: Teaches you to install and service heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration systems.
majors.about: HVAC programs cover refrigeration cycles, electrical controls, heating systems, ductwork, building automation and refrigerant handling. Technicians who handle refrigerants must earn EPA Section 608 certification, and many states license HVAC contractors.
minors: Helps you run a service company.
majors.aka: HVAC, HVACR, heating and air, refrigeration

majors.name: Plumbing and Pipefitting
majors.summary: Prepares you to install and repair water, gas, drainage and industrial piping systems.
majors.about: Plumbing and pipefitting programs teach pipe systems, codes, blueprint reading, fixtures and safety. Most plumbers learn through apprenticeships, and most states or localities license plumbers.
minors: Useful for becoming a plumbing contractor.

majors.name: Carpentry
majors.summary: Teaches you to frame, finish and build structures from wood and other materials.
majors.about: Carpentry programs cover framing, finish carpentry, cabinetry, blueprint reading, tools and safety. Many carpenters learn through apprenticeships, and the skills lead to construction lead and supervisor roles.
minors: Prepares you to lead crews and projects.
Helps if you start a contracting business.

majors.name: Mechatronics and Robotics
majors.summary: Combines mechanics, electronics and programming to build and maintain automated systems.
majors.about: Mechatronics and robotics programs teach electrical and mechanical systems, sensors, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), robotics and automation. Graduates maintain and program automated equipment in manufacturing, logistics and energy.
minors: Adds lockout and machine safety knowledge.

majors.name: Precision Machining and CNC
majors.summary: Teaches you to make precision parts with manual and computer-controlled machines.
majors.about: Precision machining programs cover blueprint reading, measurement, machining processes, CNC programming and CAD/CAM. Graduates work as machinists, CNC operators and programmers, and tool and die makers.
minors: Useful for shop supervision or ownership.
majors.aka: machinist, CNC, machine tool technology, tool and die

majors.name: Automotive Technology
majors.summary: Prepares you to diagnose and repair cars and light trucks.
majors.about: Automotive technology programs cover engines, electrical systems, brakes, suspension, climate control, diagnostics and hybrid and electric vehicles. Many align with ASE education standards and prepare students for ASE certification tests after work experience.
minors: Helps if you plan to manage or own a shop.
majors.aka: auto mechanic, automotive service, auto body, collision repair

majors.name: Diesel and Heavy Equipment Technology
majors.summary: Teaches you to maintain diesel trucks, buses and heavy equipment.
majors.about: Diesel technology programs cover diesel engines, hydraulics, electrical systems, brakes, drivetrains and preventive maintenance for trucks and heavy equipment. Graduates work for fleets, dealerships, construction firms and agriculture.
minors: Prepares you for fleet or shop management.
majors.aka: diesel mechanic, heavy equipment, truck technician, fleet maintenance

majors.name: Aviation Maintenance Technology
majors.summary: Prepares you to inspect, maintain and repair aircraft.
majors.about: Aviation maintenance programs, often at FAA-certificated schools, cover airframes, powerplants, aircraft electrical systems and regulations. Graduates can test for the FAA mechanic certificate with airframe and powerplant (A&P) ratings.

majors.name: Supply Chain Management
majors.summary: Studies how products are sourced, made, stored and delivered to customers.
majors.about: Supply chain management majors learn purchasing, inventory management, logistics, operations planning and supply chain analytics. Graduates work for manufacturers, retailers, distributors, logistics providers and government agencies.
minors: Prepares you to forecast demand and optimize inventory.
Connects supply decisions to costs and cash flow.
Prepares you to lead warehouse and distribution teams.

majors.name: Logistics and Distribution
majors.summary: Focuses on moving and storing goods efficiently through warehouses and transportation networks.
majors.about: Logistics programs focus on warehousing, distribution, transportation modes, freight and inventory systems. Programs range from certificates to bachelor's degrees, and many students already work in warehouses or transportation.
minors: Adds procurement and planning to your operations skills.
Warehouses and loading docks need safety leadership.
Prepares you for distribution center management.

majors.name: Transportation Management
majors.summary: Teaches you to plan and manage the movement of freight and passengers.
majors.about: Transportation management programs cover carriers, fleet management, transportation law, routing, safety and economics across trucking, rail, air and maritime modes.
minors: Prepares you to run a fleet or carrier operation.
Adds DOT and workplace safety knowledge.

majors.name: Operations Management
majors.summary: Studies how organizations produce goods and services efficiently and with high quality.
majors.about: Operations management majors learn process design, quality management, scheduling, inventory and lean methods. The skills apply in manufacturing, logistics, healthcare and service businesses.
minors: Helps you measure and improve processes.
Connects operations to suppliers and distribution.
Helps you manage the people who run operations.

majors.name: Aviation
majors.summary: Covers flying, airport and airline operations, and aviation management.
majors.about: Aviation programs include professional pilot training, aviation management, air traffic and airport operations. Pilots must earn FAA certificates and ratings, and airline pilots need an airline transport pilot certificate; flight training costs are often significant.
minors: Prepares you for airline and airport management.

majors.name: Elementary Education
majors.summary: Prepares you to teach children in kindergarten through the elementary grades.
majors.about: Elementary education majors learn child development, teaching methods for reading, math, science and social studies, classroom management and assessment, with supervised student teaching. Public school teachers must earn a state teaching license or certificate.
minors: Prepares you to support students with disabilities in every classroom.
Helps you work with English learners and their families.
Deepens your understanding of how children learn and behave.

majors.name: Secondary Education
majors.summary: Prepares you to teach a subject such as math, science, English or history in middle and high school.
majors.about: Secondary education majors pair a teaching subject with education courses in adolescent development, teaching methods and classroom management, plus student teaching. Teachers in public schools need a state license in their subject area.
minors: Helps you support every learner in your classes.
Math teachers are in high demand in many states.
majors.aka: high school teacher, middle school teacher, teaching

majors.name: Early Childhood Education
majors.summary: Focuses on the learning and care of children from birth to about age eight.
majors.about: Early childhood education programs cover child development, play-based learning, family engagement, health and safety, and early literacy. Credentials range from certificates and the Child Development Associate (CDA) to bachelor's degrees that lead to preschool and early elementary teaching licenses.
minors: Deepens your understanding of child development.
Prepares you to run a childcare center.
Helps you work with bilingual children and families.

majors.name: Special Education
majors.summary: Prepares you to teach and support students with disabilities.
majors.about: Special education majors learn disability characteristics, individualized education programs (IEPs), assessment, behavior support and adapted instruction. Special education teachers in public schools need a state license, and the field has had persistent teacher shortages.
minors: Helps you work with deaf and hard-of-hearing students.

majors.name: Instructional Design and Adult Learning
majors.summary: Teaches you to design training and courses for adults in workplaces and online.
majors.about: Instructional design and adult education programs cover how adults learn, course design, e-learning development, assessment and training evaluation. Graduates design and deliver training in companies, healthcare, government and colleges.
minors: Helps you create engaging course materials.
majors.aka: instructional technology, training and development, e-learning, adult education

majors.name: Biology
majors.summary: Studies living things, from cells and genes to ecosystems.
majors.about: Biology majors study cell biology, genetics, ecology, evolution and physiology, with laboratory courses throughout. The major leads to lab, research, environmental and healthcare careers and is a common path to medical, dental, veterinary and graduate school.
majors.degrees: Associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees
minors: Required by many health and research graduate programs.
Builds the data skills research depends on.

majors.name: Chemistry
majors.summary: Studies matter: what substances are made of and how they react.
majors.about: Chemistry majors study general, organic, inorganic, analytical and physical chemistry, with extensive lab work. Graduates work in labs for manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, environmental testing, food and forensics, or continue to graduate or professional school.
majors.degrees: Associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees
minors: Fits biochemistry, pharmaceutical and health careers.
Prepares you for technical sales or lab management.
Adds lab and chemical safety expertise.

majors.name: Physics
majors.summary: Studies matter, energy, motion and the fundamental laws of the universe.
majors.about: Physics majors study mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics and optics, with strong math and lab work. Graduates work in research, engineering, technology and teaching, and many go to graduate school.
minors: Supports the advanced math physics uses.
Programming is central to modern physics.
Physics teachers are in short supply.

majors.name: Mathematics
majors.summary: Studies numbers, structures, patterns and logical reasoning.
majors.about: Mathematics majors study calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, abstract algebra, analysis and statistics. Applied math tracks connect to computing, finance and engineering. Graduates work as analysts, actuaries, teachers and researchers.
minors: Opens software and data science careers.
Applies math to markets and policy.

majors.name: Forensic Science
majors.summary: Applies science to analyze evidence in criminal and civil investigations.
majors.about: Forensic science majors combine chemistry and biology with crime scene investigation, evidence handling and courtroom testimony. Many crime labs prefer degrees in chemistry or biology with forensic coursework.
minors: Explains the legal system your work supports.
Many crime labs look for a strong chemistry background.
majors.aka: crime scene investigation, CSI, criminalistics, forensics

majors.name: Geology and Earth Sciences
majors.summary: Studies the Earth: rocks, water, soil, natural resources and natural hazards.
majors.about: Geology and earth science majors study minerals, rocks, earth processes, hydrology and geophysics, with field work. Graduates work in environmental consulting, energy, mining, water resources and government agencies; some states license professional geologists.
minors: Mapping is central to earth science work.

majors.name: Criminal Justice
majors.summary: Studies crime, law enforcement, courts and corrections.
majors.about: Criminal justice majors learn criminology, criminal law, policing, corrections, juvenile justice and ethics. Graduates work in law enforcement, corrections, probation, security and the courts. Police academies and agencies set their own hiring requirements.
minors: Helps you understand behavior, crisis and mental health.
Helps you communicate with more of the community.
Explains the social roots of crime.
majors.aka: law enforcement, criminology, police science, corrections

majors.name: Fire Science
majors.summary: Studies fire behavior, prevention, firefighting and emergency response.
majors.about: Fire science programs cover fire behavior, fire prevention and codes, building construction, hazardous materials and fire service leadership. Many firefighters complete academy training and EMT certification, and fire science degrees support promotion to officer and inspector roles.
minors: Adds disaster planning and incident management.
Connects fire prevention to workplace safety.

majors.name: Emergency Management and Homeland Security
majors.summary: Prepares you to plan for, respond to and recover from disasters and emergencies.
majors.about: Emergency management and homeland security programs cover disaster planning, incident command, risk assessment, continuity planning and public safety communication. Graduates work for government agencies, hospitals, utilities, schools and private companies.
majors.degrees: Certificate, associate, bachelor's and master's degrees
minors: Connects emergency planning to workplace hazards.
majors.aka: homeland security, disaster management, emergency preparedness

majors.name: Legal Studies and Paralegal
majors.summary: Studies law and the legal system and prepares you to support attorneys.
majors.about: Legal studies and paralegal programs cover legal research and writing, civil litigation, contracts, ethics and legal technology. Paralegal certificates and associate degrees prepare students to work in law offices, while bachelor's programs are also a common route to law school.
minors: Fits corporate law and compliance work.
Bilingual paralegals can serve more clients.

majors.name: Communications
majors.summary: Studies how people create, share and interpret messages in person and through media.
majors.about: Communications majors study interpersonal, organizational, mass and digital communication, public speaking, writing and media. Graduates work in public relations, marketing, media, human resources and nonprofit organizations.
minors: Applies communication skills to business growth.
Adds video, audio and social media production.

majors.name: Journalism
majors.summary: Teaches you to report, write and produce news across print, broadcast and digital media.
majors.about: Journalism majors learn reporting, news writing, editing, media law and ethics, and multimedia storytelling. Graduates work in newsrooms, digital media, public relations and content creation.
minors: Helps you cover government and policy.

majors.name: Public Relations and Advertising
majors.summary: Studies how organizations build their reputation and persuade audiences.
majors.about: Public relations and advertising majors learn media relations, campaign planning, copywriting, crisis communication and social media strategy. Graduates work in agencies, corporate communication departments, government and nonprofits.
minors: Fits public affairs and government relations.

majors.name: Digital Media and Film Production
majors.summary: Teaches you to create video, audio, animation and interactive media.
majors.about: Digital media and film programs cover video and audio production, editing, motion graphics, storytelling and media technology. Students build a portfolio, and graduates work in production companies, broadcasting, marketing and content creation.
minors: Connects your production skills to brand content.
Useful for freelance and production company work.

majors.name: English and Professional Writing
majors.summary: Studies literature and language and builds strong writing and analysis skills.
majors.about: English and writing majors study literature, rhetoric, composition, creative and professional writing. The skills apply in publishing, technical writing, marketing, teaching and law, and the major is common preparation for law school.
minors: Applies writing to content and brand work.

majors.name: Graphic Design
majors.summary: Teaches you to communicate visually through layout, typography, images and digital media.
majors.about: Graphic design majors learn design principles, typography, layout, branding, illustration and digital design software, building a portfolio along the way. Graduates work in agencies, in-house marketing teams, publishing and freelance.
minors: Connects design to campaigns and business goals.
Lets you build the websites you design.

majors.name: Interior Design
majors.summary: Designs functional, safe and attractive interior spaces.
majors.about: Interior design majors study space planning, materials, lighting, building codes, drafting and design software. Some states regulate the title or practice of interior design, and the NCIDQ exam is the main professional credential.
minors: Helps you run a design practice.

majors.name: Fashion Design and Merchandising
majors.summary: Studies how clothing and accessories are designed, made and sold.
majors.about: Fashion programs cover design, patternmaking, textiles, garment construction, trend forecasting and fashion merchandising. Graduates work for apparel companies, retailers and as independent designers.
minors: Helps you promote collections and brands.
Helps you run a fashion business.

majors.name: Fine Arts and Studio Art
majors.summary: Develops your skills in drawing, painting, sculpture, photography and other art forms.
majors.about: Fine arts majors build technical and creative skills in studio courses along with art history and critique, finishing with a portfolio or exhibition. Graduates work as artists, in museums and galleries, in teaching and in creative industries.
majors.degrees: Associate, bachelor's (BA or BFA) and master's (MFA) degrees
minors: Helps you sell your work and manage a studio.

majors.name: Music
majors.summary: Studies music performance, theory, history, composition and production.
majors.about: Music majors take lessons and ensembles along with music theory, history and technology. Tracks include performance, education, composition and music business or production. Public school music teachers need a state license.
majors.aka: music performance, music production, music education

majors.name: Hospitality Management
majors.summary: Teaches you to manage hotels, restaurants, resorts and other guest services businesses.
majors.about: Hospitality management majors learn lodging and food and beverage operations, revenue management, guest service, event management and hospitality finance, often with internships. Graduates work for hotels, restaurants, resorts, casinos, cruise lines and event venues.
majors.degrees: Certificate, associate, bachelor's and master's degrees
minors: Helps you fill rooms and tables.
Many hospitality teams and guests speak Spanish.

majors.name: Culinary Arts
majors.summary: Teaches professional cooking, baking and kitchen management.
majors.about: Culinary arts programs teach cooking techniques, baking and pastry, food safety and sanitation, menu planning and kitchen management, with hands-on kitchen labs and often an externship.
minors: Prepares you to run a restaurant.
Helps you open your own food business.
majors.aka: culinary, chef, cooking, baking and pastry

majors.name: Tourism and Travel Management
majors.summary: Studies the business of travel, destinations and tourism experiences.
majors.about: Tourism and travel management programs cover destination marketing, tour operations, travel services, sustainable tourism and hospitality. Graduates work for travel agencies, tour companies, convention and visitor bureaus, airlines and resorts.
minors: Language skills help with travelers and destinations.

majors.name: Event Management
majors.summary: Teaches you to plan and run meetings, conferences, weddings and festivals.
majors.about: Event management programs cover event planning, budgeting, vendor management, venue operations, marketing and risk management. Graduates work for venues, hotels, agencies, associations and corporate event teams.
minors: Helps you sell and promote events.
Gives you tools to manage complex events.
majors.aka: event planning, meeting planning, conference management

majors.name: Sport and Recreation Management
majors.summary: Studies how sports programs, parks and recreation services are run.
majors.about: Sport and recreation management majors learn facility management, program planning, sport marketing, recreation leadership and parks administration. Graduates work for parks departments, athletic programs, fitness centers and sports organizations.
minors: Helps you promote programs and teams.
majors.aka: sport management, recreation, parks and recreation

majors.name: Psychology
majors.summary: Studies how people think, feel, learn and behave.
majors.about: Psychology majors study development, cognition, social behavior, mental health and research methods. A bachelor's degree leads to roles in human services, research, business and education; becoming a licensed psychologist or counselor requires graduate study and state licensure.
majors.degrees: Associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees
minors: Adds the social side of behavior.

majors.name: Social Work
majors.summary: Prepares you to help individuals, families and communities facing challenges.
majors.about: Social work majors study human behavior, social welfare policy, practice methods and ethics, with supervised field placements. A bachelor's in social work (BSW) leads to entry-level practice; clinical social work requires a master's (MSW), supervised experience and state licensure.
study: Human behavior and the social environment
minors: Deepens your understanding of mental health.
Connects social work to community health.
majors.aka: BSW, MSW, social services, case management

majors.name: Sociology
majors.summary: Studies societies, groups, institutions and social change.
majors.about: Sociology majors study social structure, inequality, families, communities and research methods. Graduates work in social services, research, nonprofits, human resources and government, and many continue to graduate school.
minors: Applies sociology to crime and justice.

majors.name: Human Services and Counseling
majors.summary: Prepares you to support people through social service and counseling programs.
majors.about: Human services and addiction counseling programs teach case management, counseling skills, crisis intervention and community resources. Many lead to entry-level human services roles, and substance abuse counselors often need state certification or licensure.
minors: Deepens your knowledge of mental health.
Helps you serve more of the community.
majors.aka: human services, addiction counseling, substance abuse counseling

majors.name: Political Science
majors.summary: Studies government, politics, public policy and international relations.
majors.about: Political science majors study American government, comparative politics, international relations, political theory and public policy. Graduates work in government, campaigns, advocacy, journalism and business, and the major is a common route to law school.
minors: Prepares you for law school and legal work.

majors.name: Public Administration and Policy
majors.summary: Teaches you to manage government agencies and nonprofit organizations.
majors.about: Public administration majors learn public budgeting, policy analysis, public management, administrative law and nonprofit management. Graduates work for local, state and federal agencies and nonprofits; the master's (MPA) is common for leadership roles.
majors.aka: MPA, public policy, government administration, nonprofit management

majors.name: History
majors.summary: Studies the past to understand how people, societies and ideas changed over time.
majors.about: History majors read primary sources, write research papers and study periods and regions around the world. Graduates work in education, museums, archives, law, government and writing, and many go on to law or graduate school.
minors: Prepares you to teach social studies.
Connects history to policy and law.

majors.name: Environmental Science and Sustainability
majors.summary: Studies the environment and how to protect natural resources and human health.
majors.about: Environmental science majors combine biology, chemistry, earth science and policy to study pollution, ecosystems, climate and natural resources, with field and lab work. Graduates work for environmental consulting firms, government agencies, industry and nonprofits.
minors: Mapping is used across environmental careers.
Connects environmental work to hazardous waste and worker safety.
Connects the environment to human health.

majors.name: Occupational Safety and Health
majors.summary: Teaches you to identify workplace hazards and protect workers from injury and illness.
majors.about: Occupational safety and health programs cover OSHA regulations, hazard recognition, industrial hygiene, ergonomics, fire protection, accident investigation and safety management systems. Graduates work as safety specialists in construction, manufacturing, energy, healthcare and government. Professional certifications such as the CSP require experience and exams.
majors.degrees: Certificate, associate, bachelor's and master's degrees
minors: Helps you make the business case for safety.
Connects worker safety to environmental compliance.
Construction is a major employer of safety professionals.
majors.aka: OSHA, safety management, industrial hygiene, EHS, environmental health and safety

majors.name: Renewable Energy Technology
majors.summary: Prepares you to install, maintain and manage solar, wind and other clean energy systems.
majors.about: Renewable energy programs cover electrical fundamentals, solar photovoltaic systems, wind turbines, energy storage, energy efficiency and safety. Graduates work as installers and technicians and in energy auditing and project development.
minors: Helps with project development and sales.
Broadens your view of clean energy policy.
majors.aka: solar, wind energy, clean energy, energy technology

majors.name: Agriculture and Agribusiness
majors.summary: Studies how food, fiber and plants are produced, managed and sold.
majors.about: Agriculture majors study crop and soil science, animal production, agricultural economics, farm management and agricultural technology. Graduates work on farms and ranches, in agribusiness, food companies, extension services and government agencies.
majors.degrees: Certificate, associate, bachelor's and master's degrees
minors: Helps you run a farm or agribusiness.

majors.name: Animal Science and Veterinary Technology
majors.summary: Studies animal biology, care, nutrition and health.
majors.about: Animal science majors study animal nutrition, genetics, reproduction and management. Veterinary technology programs, usually associate degrees, prepare students to assist veterinarians; most states credential veterinary technicians, typically after the national VTNE exam.
minors: Useful for running a farm or animal business.
majors.aka: vet tech, veterinary technology, pre-vet, animal science

majors.name: Forestry and Natural Resources
majors.summary: Studies how to manage forests, wildlife, parks and natural resources.
majors.about: Forestry and natural resources majors study forest ecology, wildlife management, conservation, fire management and resource policy, with field work. Graduates work for forest services, parks, conservation agencies and timber companies.
minors: Mapping is central to resource management.
